questions.q:
Rectangle P measures 6 cm by 4 cm. Rectangle Q is mathematically similar to P. The longer side of Q is 15 cm.
Find the length of the shorter side of Q.
questions.tip: Match corresponding sides: longer with longer, shorter with shorter.

questions.q:
(a) Triangle PQR has PQ = 5 cm, angle PQR = 40° and QR = 7 cm.
Triangle XYZ has XY = 5 cm, angle XYZ = 40° and YZ = 7 cm.
Write down the condition that shows the triangles are congruent. [1]
(b) Explain why two triangles with the same three angles are not necessarily congruent. [1]
ms: (a) B1: SAS (two sides and the included angle)
(b) B1: they are similar but can be different sizes (one can be an enlargement of the other)
questions.model:
(a) SAS: two sides and the angle between them are equal.
(b) Equal angles only make the triangles similar; one could be an enlargement of the other, so the sides need not be equal.
questions.tip: AAA is a test for similarity, not congruence.

questions.q:
In triangle PQR, S is a point on PQ and T is a point on PR. ST is parallel to QR.
PS = 6 cm, SQ = 4 cm, QR = 12.5 cm and PT = 4.5 cm.
(a) Find ST. [2]
(b) Find TR. [2]
questions.model:
Triangles PST and PQR are similar (ST ∥ QR). PQ = 6 + 4 = 10 cm.
(a) ST = 12.5 × 6/10 = 7.5 cm.
(b) PR = 4.5 × 10/6 = 7.5 cm, so TR = 7.5 − 4.5 = 3 cm.
questions.tip: Use PQ = 10, not SQ = 4: compare the whole small triangle with the whole large triangle.

questions.q:
Two containers are mathematically similar. Their capacities are 1.6 litres and 5.4 litres.
(a) The label on the larger container has area 117 cm². Find the area of the label on the smaller container. [3]
(b) The height of the smaller container is 12 cm. Find the height of the larger container. [1]
ms: (a) M1: linear factor 3/2 and area factor 9/4 (2.25)
(b) B1: 18 cm FT their linear factor
questions.model:
(a) Volume scale factor = 5.4 ÷ 1.6 = 3.375 = 27/8, so the linear scale factor = ∛(27/8) = 3/2.
Area scale factor = (3/2)² = 9/4.
Smaller label = 117 ÷ 9/4 = 52 cm².
(b) 12 × 3/2 = 18 cm.
questions.tip: Always go back to the linear scale factor k first, then square or cube it.

questions.q:
A solid cone has height 24 cm. A small cone of height 8 cm is cut off the top by a cut parallel to the base, leaving a frustum.
The volume of the original cone is 1215 cm³.
(a) Calculate the volume of the frustum. [3]
(b) The curved surface area of the original cone is 540 cm². Find the curved surface area of the small cone. [2]
ms: (a) M1: scale factor 1/3 (8/24) and volume factor 1/27
questions.model:
(a) The small cone is similar to the original with k = 8/24 = 1/3.
Volume of small cone = 1215 × (1/3)³ = 1215 ÷ 27 = 45 cm³.
Frustum = 1215 − 45 = 1170 cm³.
(b) Area factor = (1/3)² = 1/9. Curved surface area = 540 ÷ 9 = 60 cm².
questions.tip: The cut-off cone is similar to the original, so you can use k³ instead of the cone formula.

questions.q:
A field is a triangle with sides 120 m, 90 m and 75 m. A scale drawing of the field is made using a scale of 1 : 1500.
(a) Calculate the lengths of the three sides on the scale drawing, in centimetres. [2]
(b) Describe how to construct the triangle accurately using a ruler and compasses only. [2]
(c) A pond on the scale drawing has an area of 2 cm². Calculate the real area of the pond in m². [2]
ms: (a) M1: converts metres to cm and divides by 1500, e.g. 12 000 ÷ 1500
(b) B1: draw one side (e.g. 8 cm) with a ruler, then with compasses draw an arc of radius 6 cm from one end and an arc of radius 5 cm from the other end
(b) B1: join the point where the arcs cross to both ends, leaving the construction arcs visible
questions.model:
(a) 120 m = 12 000 cm, 12 000 ÷ 1500 = 8 cm. Similarly 9000 ÷ 1500 = 6 cm and 7500 ÷ 1500 = 5 cm.
(b) Draw the 8 cm side with a ruler. Open the compasses to 6 cm and draw an arc from one end; open them to 5 cm and draw an arc from the other end. Join the intersection of the arcs to each end of the 8 cm line. Leave all arcs showing.
(c) Area scale factor = 1500². Real area = 2 × 1500² = 4 500 000 cm² = 450 m² (1 m² = 10 000 cm²).
questions.tip: Areas scale by the square of the map scale, and 1 m² = 10 000 cm², not 100 cm².
